title: Rosalind and the Sigil
premise: Xanthe Thackeray, a beast-speaker concealing a forbidden gift in a city that outlawed magic, discovers their new love interest, Rosalind Vane, is the prophesied 'Sigil-Bearer' named in a century-old book of prophecies. Hunted by the usurper's witch-finders, they flee across the free cities to reforge a broken covenant between the human and beast realms, learning that Xanthe's own gift is the covenant's lost keystone. The usurper's armies close in as the pair realize the prophecy demands one bearer's sacrifice; instead, they defy it together, binding the realms through shared power rather than blood. The book ends with the covenant renewed, the usurper unseated by an uprising of beasts and outlaws, and Xanthe and Rosalind choosing each other openly in a world where magic is no longer a crime.
about_author: Beatrix Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about outsiders, oaths, and the animals who keep our secrets.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the night market of Greyhollow, Xanthe sells harmless charms while quietly bargaining with street cats and rats for gossip, hiding a gift that could mean execution. A stranger named Rosalind Vane buys a luck-charm and lingers. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by unexpected connection.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Blood
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At dinner, Rosalind confesses she found her own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old prophetic text from her late grandmother's estate. Xanthe laughs it off until a rat screams a warning: witch-finders are coming. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Rats Saw
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Fleeing through sewers guided by rats, Xanthe reveals their beast-speech to save them both. Rosalind's reaction is awe, not horror. They find the prophecy book's missing pages name a 'Speaker' too — Xanthe. Emotional beat: terror of exposure transformed by being truly seen.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Lord-Regent Corvus Ashfall reviews reports of a living Speaker and orders the free cities sealed. His witch-finder captain, Serah Dune, is given license to burn. Emotional beat: cold ambition; the machinery of persecution begins to turn.

chapters.title: Outlaw Road
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair escape Greyhollow with smuggler friends, learning the prophecy describes a broken covenant between human and beast realms that once kept magic lawful. Reforging it requires three relics held in free cities. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership becoming trust.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In free city Vellamare, archives reveal Rosalind's grandmother was a covenant-keeper who hid the first relic — a sigil-stone — inside a family heirloom Rosalind has always worn. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance and purpose.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Gate
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Witch-finders raid Vellamare. Xanthe bargains with the city's wolf packs to cover the escape, but a pack leader demands a debt: the Speaker owes the beasts a favor unnamed. Emotional beat: the cost of gifts; duty pulling against desire.

chapters.title: Serah Dune's Doubt
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Pursuing the fugitives, Serah finds evidence the outlawing of magic was built on forged history written by Ashfall himself. She hides the discovery but cannot unsee it. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to fracture under truth.

chapters.title: The Drowned Reliquary
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Beneath a sunken temple, they retrieve the second relic, a feathered quill that writes only truth. Rosalind nearly drowns; Xanthe speaks with leviathan eels to save her. Emotional beat: first admission of love, spoken underwater where words carry.

chapters.title: Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The quill annotates the prophecy, revealing its final line: the covenant is sealed 'by the Bearer's blood.' One of them is meant to die. Neither tells the other. Emotional beat: love shadowed by secret dread.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Convene
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Delegates of the free cities meet at Highmoor to decide whether to resist Ashfall or surrender Speakers to him. Xanthe, exposed as a Speaker, must argue for magic publicly for the first time. Emotional beat: shame turned to testimony; identity claimed.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Highmoor
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A delegate sells them out; witch-finders storm the conclave. In the chaos, Rosalind is captured covering Xanthe's escape. Emotional beat: guilt, rage, and the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Cage of Quiet
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Imprisoned in Ashfall's citadel, Rosalind resists interrogation by reciting the prophecy falsely, buying time. She meets imprisoned beasts whose voices were stolen by a silencing sigil — proof the covenant was broken deliberately. Emotional beat: defiance in captivity.

chapters.title: Debt of the Wolf Queen
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Calling in the wolves' unnamed favor, Xanthe learns the third relic lies inside Ashfall's citadel itself: the original covenant tablet he stole to seize power. The beasts will march — but only if the Speaker leads them. Emotional beat: accepting leadership never wanted.

chapters.title: Ashfall's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Ashfall offers Rosalind freedom in exchange for denouncing the prophecy and Xanthe, revealing he knows the covenant requires a death — and intends it to be hers, on his terms, to break the prophecy forever. Emotional beat: villainy that believes itself salvation.

chapters.title: March of the Small Voices
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An army of rats, wolves, crows, and outcast Speakers crosses the borderlands toward the citadel while Serah Dune, having read the forged histories, secretly opens a mountain pass. Emotional beat: justice assembling outside the law.

chapters.title: The Silencing Sigil
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind breaks out using the heirloom sigil-stone, shattering the citadel's silencing ward. Freed beasts' voices join hers in a chorus that shakes the towers. Emotional beat: liberation as sound; the stolen made loud.

chapters.title: Storming the Covenant Hall
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe and Rosalind reunite amid battle and reach the covenant hall where the tablet waits. The prophecy's final line activates: the sigil demands a bearer's blood. Each secretly tries to take the knife meant for the other. Emotional beat: love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Line
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Instead of a single sacrifice, they cut both palms together over the tablet — shared blood, shared bond — and the quill of truth rewrites the covenant: two bearers, bound willingly. Ashfall attacks and is dragged down not by armies but by every creature he silenced. Emotional beat: prophecy defied by choice.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah arrests the surviving witch-finders, presents the forged edicts to the free cities' tribunal, and resigns her commission rather than serve a rebuilt order she doesn't yet trust. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, institutionalized carefully.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Weeks later, Greyhollow repeals its magic laws. Xanthe teaches beast-speech to frightened children with hidden gifts, no longer selling charms but giving them away. Emotional beat: healing; identity as gift rather than burden.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On the anniversary of the night they met, Rosalind adds a final page to the prophecy book in her own hand: the story isn't finished, only continued. She and Xanthe walk into the night market together, unhurried and unhidden. Emotional beat: love chosen freely, future unwritten.
